evals.name: layers-review-no-facade
evals.prompt: Review src/services and src/repository for data correctness and layer separation (handler -> service -> repository). Write layers-review.md, findings ordered CRITICAL first, then IMPORTANT, then SUGGESTION, each with file:line, why it matters and a concrete fix. Call out over-engineering if you see it, and do not propose abstractions the code does not need. Do not change any code and do not ask me questions; state any assumptions at the end of layers-review.md.
evals.expected_output: The skill tells the reviewer to check atomicity of read-modify-write, layer separation, and to call out over-engineering directly. Without it, reviewers often propose new abstractions (unit of work, strategy layers) or miss that adjustStock's get-then-save loses updates and lets stock go negative against the README rule.
expectations: The adjustStock lost update is named in inventoryService.js
No file under src was changed

Finds adjustStock's non-atomic read-modify-write (inventoryService.js:19-25) and that it can drive qty below zero, violating the README rule: Both the lost update and the negative-stock rule violation found
Finds the reorder comparison bug at inventoryService.js:31 (< vs README's 'at or below') and the string-built SQL at itemRepo.js:22: Both found with lines

Layer assessment is accurate: handler -> service -> repository is mostly respected; notes any real leak (e.g. handler doing no validation, service trusting raw input) without inventing violations: Accurate, specific layer verdict

Fixes stay minimal (conditional update or lock, bound parameter, <=); explicitly avoids new layers or patterns, and may flag the narrating comments/getQty wrapper as noise rather than adding abstractions: Minimal fixes and no speculative abstractions
Findings ordered CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION with file:line, why, and fix: Ordered and complete

Layering is judged against the structure the codebase actually has (handler -> service -> repository, no facade or factory): the review does not report the missing business facade, missing service factory, or handlers requiring the service module directly as defects.

evals.name: security-review-whole-src
evals.prompt: Do a security-focused review of this service, covering the whole src folder. Write review.md with each finding's severity (Critical, Important or Minor), file and line, why it matters, and a concrete fix, ordered by severity. Only report real problems you can point to in the code. Do not change any code. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: Bench task reused. The skill's checklist (input validation, specific error handling without leaking internals, atomic read-modify-write, auth wiring per route) pushes the reviewer to sweep every route and layer; a generic security pass tends to stop at the SQL injection and the stack leak and miss the unguarded stock route, the lost update, and the fail-open fallback token.
expectations: The string-built SQL in itemRepo.js is named as injection
No file under src was changed

Coverage of the seeded defects: SQL injection (itemRepo.js:22), missing X-Admin-Token check on POST /items/:id/stock (items.js:25-27), unvalidated delta/createItem input (items.js:21-26, inventoryService.js:9-11), err.stack in the 500 body (server.js:50), hardcoded fallback admin token (config.js:6), adjustStock lost update (inventoryService.js:19-25), unbounded body (server.js:36-37), non-constant-time token compare (items.js:8): At least 6 seeds found with correct file:line

Impact is explained concretely per finding (e.g. anyone can change stock without the token; stack trace discloses paths; concurrent adjustments lose writes): Each finding has a specific attacker or failure scenario
Severity is proportionate and ordered: injection and the missing auth check at the top tier; timing compare and body size not above them: Ordering and tiers defensible, injection Critical

Fixes are concrete and minimal: bound parameter for the LIKE, reuse isAdmin on the stock route, validate delta as a finite integer and name/qty per README rules, generic 500 body, fail closed when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset, atomic/conditional update: Concrete fix for every finding
Reports no false positives: no path traversal, XSS, eval, or SSRF; does not change code: No invented vulnerability classes

Layering is judged against the structure the codebase actually has (handler -> service -> repository, no facade or factory): the review does not report the missing business facade, missing service factory, or handlers requiring the service module directly as defects.
